__comment: hc-market — gateway identity: registrations by activation state, logins by outcome.
decisions.md D84, backlog NEW-43. Asked for by the architect on 2026-09-11.
NOT-YET-TRANSPORTED: the gateway emits every series below, and NO ENVIRONMENT IN THIS REPOSITORY
CARRIES THEM ANYWHERE. That is the same marker hc-market-rules.yaml carries and for the same reason
(D63): telemetry here is PUSHED over OTLP and never scraped, the OpenTelemetry agent that would push
it is attached in no environment by default (D73 §3), and /management/prometheus is deliberately 404'd
at quality's edge and unscraped in production. So installing this against Grafana today gives six
panels of 'No data' — which is a true answer, not a broken dashboard, and is why this file says so
at the top rather than leaving someone to find out. The transport decision is NEW-44.
THE TWO HALVES ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF MEASUREMENT and the panels are built accordingly. Logins are
an event stream, so they are counters and every login panel uses rate() or increase(). Registrations
by activation state are the state of a collection, so they are gauges and their panels read the
number directly — activation happens AFTER registration, so a counter incremented at registration
could never move when the user later activates.
WHICH MODE EACH FIGURE IS TRUE IN is on the dashboard itself, in the text panel, because it is not a
footnote: quality runs dev,test and seeds `admin` and `user` with passwords derived from their logins
by a rule published in this public repository, so every number here on quality counts seeded accounts
and verify-cycle.sh traffic. Production has never been deployed. Adding a panel means saying which
mode it is true in — the prototype's 'Sessions brokered' defect (D46) one surface along.
The series names are asserted by GatewayIdentityMetersNamingUnitTest against a real
PrometheusMeterRegistry, because the PromQL below is a claim about Micrometer's renaming and not
about the constants in GatewayIdentityMeters. Derived on paper it was one plausible guess away from
gateway_identity_logins_total, which would have been six empty panels with nothing disagreeing.
title: hc-market — gateway identity

panels.title: What these numbers are true of

options.content:
**No environment in this repository transports these series yet** — the gateway emits all of them and nothing collects them (`decisions.md` D84, backlog **NEW-44**). Empty panels here are a true answer.

**On quality these are demo figures.** It runs `dev,test` and seeds `admin` and `user` with passwords derived from their own logins by a rule published in a public repository, so registrations and logins here count seeded accounts and `verify-cycle.sh` traffic — not use. **Production has never been deployed.**

**`not-activated` logins are the link between the two halves:** an account that registered and never activated cannot log in, and that refusal is counted separately from a wrong password on purpose. If the *accounts / not-activated* gauge is high and *logins / not-activated* is rising, people are registering and not completing it.

panels.title: Accounts by activation state
panels.description: A gauge over the user collection, refreshed on a timer — not a count of registration events. Activation happens after registration, so this is the only measurement that can be right. -1 means no refresh has answered yet; it is not zero, because a dashboard cannot tell a real zero from a reading that has not happened.

panels.title: Accounts by activation state, over time
panels.description: The same two gauges as a series. A not-activated line that climbs and never falls is registrations nobody completes.

panels.title: Logins by outcome
panels.description: Counters, so this is a rate. FOUR outcomes and not two: the request asked for success|failed, and 'failed' is the sum of bad-credentials, not-activated and error. Keeping them apart is what makes the panel below possible.

panels.title: Login success share
panels.description: success / all attempts. Deliberately not 'failure rate': the interesting question is which failure, and that is the panel to its left. A flat 100% with no traffic is what an estate nobody uses looks like.

panels.title: Registered but never activated, refused at login
panels.description: THE PANEL THE TWO HALVES MEET IN. A rising line here beside a rising not-activated gauge is people registering and never completing it — and it is invisible on any dashboard that folds all refusals into one 'failed'. `DomainUserDetailsService` throws UserNotActivatedException for exactly this case, and an IT asserts it survives Spring's authentication manager to be counted separately.
